map.128 bit = 48 bit 时间戳（毫秒，大端）+ 80 bit 随机: 128 bit = 48 bit timestamp (milliseconds, big-endian) + 80 bit random
map.ULID 用 128 位表示：前 48 位是毫秒级 Unix 时间戳（大端），后: A ULID uses 128 bits: the first 48 bits are a millisecond Unix timestamp (big-endian), the last 80 bits are cryptographically secure random values. The string form encodes to 26 Crockford Base32 characters (dropping I, L, O, U to avoid confusion and dirty words, case-insensitive). The high-order timestamp makes ULIDs sort lexicographically by generation time by nature, usable directly as a database primary key or sort key, while avoiding exposing business scale via auto-increment IDs. The 80 random bits guarantee about 1.2×10²⁴ values per millisecond — collision negligible.

map.不敏感，字母表排除 I L O U 防误读。: Not sensitive; the alphabet excludes I L O U to prevent misreading.
map.概率极低。ULID 的后 80 位是随机值，同一毫秒内约 1.2×10²⁴ 种取: Extremely unlikely. The last 80 bits of a ULID are random, giving about 1.2×10²⁴ values per millisecond; even generating a million IDs per second, the collision probability is negligible. But note: if a large batch is generated within the same millisecond and the implementation is flawed (e.g., improper random source, counter not incremented correctly), collisions can still occur — use a mature library.
